## Neutrino observatories {#icecube-future}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### IceCube

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
**South Pole, Antarctic ice**

**IceCube:** $1\,\mathrm{km}^3$, operating.

**Upgrade:** 5 new strings, installed in 2026.

**Gen2:** $8\,\mathrm{km}^3$ optical array, proposed.

**Measurement:** more high-energy events; improved calibration and a radio extension.
:::

:::
:::

### KM3NeT

[]{#km3net-arca-orca}

::::: {.columns}

**Mediterranean Sea**

**ARCA:** $\sim1\,\mathrm{km}^3$ for neutrino astronomy.

**ORCA:** $\sim7\,\mathrm{Mt}$ for neutrino oscillations.

**Full design:** 230 / 115 strings.

Construction and data taking.

**Measurement:** source searches with ARCA; oscillations with ORCA.

::: {.notes}
Observatories and prospects occupy 47–56 minutes. After the sensitivity scaling
and sky coverage, use the IceCube, KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD tabs. The four proposed
arrays are reserve comparisons; their volumes are not a performance ranking.
Scientific goals here are goals, not measured sensitivity improvements.

IceCube uses one cubic kilometre of instrumented ice. The collaboration's
12 February 2026 deployment announcement reports five additional Upgrade
strings, with commissioning following installation. Older seven-string
plans are not the installed configuration. Gen2's eight cubic kilometres
refer to the proposed optical array, not the radio footprint or an existing
detector. The accompanying figure is a design visualization.
Sources: [IceCube Upgrade deployment](https://icecube.wisc.edu/news/press-releases/2026/02/the-icecube-neutrino-observatory-gets-a-major-upgrade-beneath-the-ice/)
and [IceCube-Gen2 detectors](https://icecube-gen2.wisc.edu/facility/detectors/).

KM3NeT: all displayed sizes and string counts are the full design. ARCA
contains two blocks of 115 detection units. ORCA has one block and about
seven megatonnes of instrumented seawater. The picture compares their
horizontal footprints, not volumes. Both arrays take data during construction.
Sources: [ARCA](https://www.km3net.org/research/physics/astronomy-with-arca/),
[ORCA](https://www.km3net.org/research/physics/particle-physics-with-orca/),
[array comparison](https://www.km3net.org/research/detector/arca-and-orca-detector/).

Baikal-GVD: the collaboration's 2026 description reports 16 independent
clusters and an effective volume of 0.8 cubic kilometres. This published
effective-volume number has no energy/event-selection definition on that
page and must not be equated to the geometric instrumented volumes of other
arrays. The separate EXP cluster in the drawing tests technologies and is
not a seventeenth physics cluster. Original labels and depth conventions in
the drawing are retained. Source: [Baikal-GVD](https://baikal-gvd.jinr.ru/telescope).

P-ONE: the baseline is seven clusters of ten strings, for approximately one
cubic kilometre. The drawing is a schematic design, with dimensions from
its original version, not an as-built survey. The August 2026 ONC update
describes engineering tests and a planned first-line deployment later that
year. It does not establish completion of that deployment. The full array
is not claimed to be operating.
Sources: [P-ONE design](https://www.pacific-neutrino.org/p-one/),
[ONC engineering update, 15 August 2026](https://www.oceannetworks.ca/news-and-stories/stories/onc-coengineers-key-infrastructure-for-pacific-deep-sea-neutrino-telescope/).

TRIDENT: the displayed numbers belong to the 2023 full-array proposal.
The 1,211 strings use hybrid PMT/SiPM sensors and instrument a geometric
volume of about 7.5 cubic kilometres. The layout follows Penrose tiling and
includes paths for remotely operated maintenance vehicles. A pathfinder
is distinct from that full configuration. No simulated sensitivity or
angular-resolution number is presented as measured performance.
Source: [Ye et al. (2023)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-023-02087-6).

HUNT: the approximately 30-cubic-kilometre size is a proposed scale; details,
prototypes and sources are on the next slide (`b-hunt`). B-HUNT is the Baikal
option of HUNT, not an independent extra capacity to add to HUNT.
Project source: [IHEP](https://ihep.cas.cn/astro/en/research/sf/ucp/202510/t20251011_7986821.html);
large-PMT technology: [Peng et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09910).

NEON: the 2025 revision proposes a ten-cubic-kilometre cylindrical array
with 1,200 strings and multi-PMT modules. The upper panel of Figure 3 shows
the candidate Fibonacci-spiral geometry. Hardware testing does not establish
an operating full array. Source: [Zhang et al., arXiv:2408.05122v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05122v3).

Image credits and original files: `media/observatories/SOURCES.md`.
:::

## Baikal-GVD → B-HUNT {#b-hunt}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### From GVD to B-HUNT

![](media/prospects/gvd-to-bhunt.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-width: 1450px; --media-max-height: 580px;" fig-alt="Milestones: 2024 first HUNT prototype string in Lake Baikal with 12 modules of 20-inch photomultipliers; 2025 a full-scale string with 20-inch modules operating in Lake Baikal, and four prototype detector units with an LED calibration unit at 1600 metres in the South China Sea; 2026 Baikal-GVD with 16 clusters and about 0.8 cubic kilometres effective volume; about 2028 Baikal-GVD at about 1 cubic kilometre; about 2040 B-HUNT at about 30 cubic kilometres. Two cubes of 1 and 30 cubic kilometres are drawn to volume scale."}

::: {.media-caption}
Russia + China · Baikal-GVD Collaboration with IHEP (Beijing) · [JINR (2026)](https://www.jinr.ru/posts/grigory-trubnikov-baikal-gvd-neutrino-telescope-to-reach-1-km-sup-3-sup-volume-by-2028/) · [IHEP](https://ihep.cas.cn/astro/en/research/sf/ucp/202510/t20251011_7986821.html)
:::

### Why Baikal?

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="47%"}
**The ice is a platform:** strings are deployed from the frozen lake every winter.

**Water:** light scatters less than in ice, so cascade directions are sharper.

**Northern site:** the Galactic Centre is below the horizon $75\%$ of the day.

**A gamma-ray partner:** LHAASO watches the same northern sky.

Alerts and follow-up: work in progress.
:::
::: {.column width="49%"}
![](media/observatories/hunt-design.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 520px;" fig-alt="Official HUNT concept illustration showing large single-PMT optical modules on underwater strings. This is a design illustration, not a photograph of an operating array."}

::: {.media-caption}
[Design illustration. HUNT / IHEP, CAS.](https://ihep.cas.cn/astro/en/research/sf/ucp/202510/t20251011_7986821.html)
:::
:::
:::::

::::::

::: {.notes}
**Say:** Baikal-GVD is now close to a cubic kilometre, and together with our Chinese colleagues we are already testing the next step in the lake — B-HUNT, a telescope thirty times bigger, built on the same ice that made Baikal neutrino astronomy possible.

Allow about two minutes. The project name used in this lecture is B-HUNT: the
Baikal option of HUNT (High-energy Underwater Neutrino Telescope), proposed by the
LHAASO team of IHEP (Beijing) with a volume of about 30 cubic kilometres; IHEP
describes it as relying on LHAASO, Deep Network China and Baikal-GVD
([IHEP, 11 October 2025](https://ihep.cas.cn/astro/en/research/sf/ucp/202510/t20251011_7986821.html)).
IHEP presents two candidate sites for HUNT: Lake Baikal (2212 strings, 720 m high, 3.8 km
radius, at about 1300 m depth) and the South China Sea (M. Chen, RICH 2025,
15 September 2025). JINR announces that by 2040 a 30-cubic-kilometre HUNT
telescope will be built in Lake Baikal by the Baikal-GVD Collaboration jointly
with IHEP ([JINR, 3 March 2026](https://www.jinr.ru/posts/grigory-trubnikov-baikal-gvd-neutrino-telescope-to-reach-1-km-sup-3-sup-volume-by-2028/),
G. V. Trubnikov and Zh.-A. M. Dzhilkibaev). On 10 October 2026 MSU Rector
V. A. Sadovnichy announced MSU's participation in the Russia–China project; that
news item gives "30 km²", whereas the project documents give a volume of about
30 km³, used here.

Milestones. March 2024: first HUNT prototype string in Lake Baikal with 12 optical
modules housing 20-inch PMTs
([C. Liu et al., PoS(ICRC2025)1101](https://doi.org/10.22323/1.501.1101)).
2025 expedition: a prototype string of the next-generation telescope deployed
jointly with IHEP, and a full-scale string with modules based on 20-inch PMTs
put into operation ([JINR, 1 April 2025](https://www.jinr.ru/posts/2025-expedition-to-deploy-baikal-gvd-telescope-completed/));
IHEP's slides give 24 modules for March 2025. January 2025, South China Sea:
four detector units and one LED calibration unit placed at 1600 m and connected to
the national seafloor observation network
([Science and Technology Daily, 5 February 2025](https://www.stdaily.com/web/gdxw/2025-02/05/content_293176.html)).
The 2026 plan includes another HUNT prototype string (JINR weekly, 5 March 2026).

Baikal-GVD: 16 clusters and 0.8 cubic kilometres effective volume in 2026
([Baikal-GVD](https://baikal-gvd.jinr.ru/telescope)); after the 2025 expedition
JINR quoted 0.7 cubic kilometres and set one cubic kilometre as the goal for 2028.
Effective volume (GVD) and instrumented volume (HUNT) are different quantities; the
cubes compare only the stated sizes.

Why Baikal. Deployment from the ice cover in winter has been the basis of the
Baikal technique since NT-200 (slide on Baikal beginnings). Light scatters less in
lake water than in Antarctic ice, which sharpens cascade directions. For example,
the eight Baikal-GVD cascades above 200 TeV have 50%-containment radii of
1.6–3.3 degrees ([ApJ 982, 73 (2025), Table 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05608)),
whereas the 2013 IceCube contained showers had a typical median angular resolution
of 10–15 degrees ([Science 342 (2013)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.5238v2)).
Treat this as an illustration only: the samples, energies, reconstructions and
definitions differ, and IceCube's cascade reconstruction has improved since. The 75% is the fraction of a sidereal day the Galactic Centre spends
below the horizon at the Baikal site (geometry only; see the sky-coverage tab).
LHAASO, in the Northern Hemisphere, detects ultra-high-energy gamma-ray sources
in the Galactic plane, natural neutrino targets. Alerts and follow-up for GVD:
say only that this work is in progress.

Figure generator, tests and the full milestone table: `assets/prospects/`.
:::
